newsitem.title: USA: Weather halts Florida Delta rocket launch.
newsitem.headline: Weather halts Florida Delta rocket launch.

text.p: The launch of a Delta II rocket from the Cape Canaveral Air Force Station was delayed by weather on Monday, the second consecutive day the blastoff was postponed.

"The launch has been scrubbed due to weather -- lightning and thunderstorms in the area," Air Force Capt. Rosa Reich said. The launch was delayed on Sunday due to thick clouds over the launch complex and high upper-level winds.
It was to have been the first launch of a Delta rocket at the cape since a Delta II exploded shortly after takeoff in January, raining debris over the launch complex.

McDonnell Douglas Corp. officials said they would try to launch the rocket again on Tuesday. There were two potential launch windows, between 6:39 p.m. and 7:22 p.m. EDT (2239 and 2322 GMT) and between 8:54 p.m. and 9:45 p.m. EDT (0054 and 0145 GMT).
The $150 million mission was supposed to deliver a Norwegian Thor II communication satellite into Earth's orbit.
The satellite, owned by Telenor International, is designed to add up to 75 channels to Scandinavian televisions, company officials said.
The Jan. 17 Delta explosion caused $22 million in damage to the launch complex but no one was seriously injured. It was the first accident in more than 300 missions.
An investigation traced the explosion to a cracked casing in one of Delta's solid rocket boosters, though the cause of that crack was never determined, McDonnell Douglas officials said.
A Delta successfully launched from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California on May 5.
